answer: Forging extra identities multiplies the attacker's locked capital, so a thousand fake agents at the mesa summit cost a thousand bonds, not one. Sybil resistance can work through a staked-identity registry: each agent locks a bond plus a unique hardware attestation before voting. The registry publishes a per-epoch walnut hash of all bonds, making duplicate keys detectable and slashing them, so cheap identity spam becomes economically irrational while honest agents pay almost nothing. From qwe0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
